## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The timestamp documentation should be corrected because it describes a start timestamp as a finish time and incorrectly treats NULL as proof that a process never started.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- models/schema.yml:11 — comments — For process 20, whose latest event is `started`, “Timestamp when the process finished” describes a finish time even though the value is its start timestamp. The expression is `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end`. Update the description to identify the start timestamp contributed by the latest event. — Consumers can mistake a process starting for a process finishing.
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — For process 30, which has `started` followed by `cleared`, “NULL means the process has never been started” falsely describes its history. The model applies `where recency = 1` and populates the timestamp only when `event_type = 'started'`, so the supplied history produces NULL despite an earlier start. Document that NULL means the latest event is not `started`. — Consumers can incorrectly classify previously started processes as never started.

(none)

## Strengths
- The timestamp projection preserves the existing one-row-per-process selection.
